match.reason: No point in the bank defines marketing itself; the closest, market research for a new business, is a narrower and different idea.

draft.title: What marketing is
card: Marketing is finding out what customers want and then getting it to them at a profit. It starts with the customer, not with the product.
A business finds out what customers want through market research, such as surveys and sales data. It then uses what it learns to decide what to make and sell.
Getting the product to customers includes its price, where and how it is sold, and how people hear about it.
Advertising is only one part of this. Marketing also covers research, product design, pricing and distribution. A business must also earn a profit, not just satisfy customers.
draft.remember: Marketing means meeting customer wants at a profit. Advertising is one small part of it.

opts: Finding out what customers want and supplying it at a profit
Telling as many people as possible about a product
Making a product as cheaply as the business can
Persuading customers to buy whatever is already made
a.why: Marketing begins with what customers want and ends with supplying it at a profit. Telling people about a product is only advertising, which is one part of marketing.
a.clue: Marketing starts with the customer and still needs a profit.

b.q: Priya runs a bakery in Orange. Surveys show her customers want more gluten-free bread, so she bakes it, prices it and stocks it in her shop. Why is this marketing, not just advertising?
opts: She researched wants, then supplied the product at a profit
She promoted her bakery to more people in the town
She cut her costs by baking larger batches each day
She sold bread that she already knew how to make
b.why: Priya found out what customers wanted and then supplied it, which is the core of marketing. Promoting the bakery to more people would be advertising, and that is only one part of marketing.
b.clue: Look at what she did before she made the bread.

a.best: Finding out what customers want and supplying it at a profit

b.best: She researched wants, then supplied the product at a profit

problems.detail: The right option says Priya supplied the bread 'at a profit', but the scenario never says she made a profit. It only says she baked, priced and stocked it. The option asserts something the stem does not establish.
